title: Figma keyboard shortcuts Mac: how designers remember them and fix conflicts in 2026
metaTitle: Figma keyboard shortcuts Mac: remember them and fix conflicts
description: Remember Figma keyboard shortcuts on Mac with Figma's shortcuts panel, App Shortcuts in System Settings and a short daily routine. Free fixes first.
intro: Figma keyboard shortcuts Mac users need are mostly the Command keys you already know. Figma lists the rest in its shortcuts panel, which opens with ⌃⇧?. Start with the panel, then fix the few keys that fight your habits, using free Mac settings and a short daily routine.
tldr: Open Figma's shortcuts panel with ⌃⇧? and use it as your reference, not your memory.
Learn five keys at a time. Habit research points to weeks, not days.
For menu commands you use daily, add an App Shortcut in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts.
Check your keyboard layout in the panel's Layout tab before you blame a key.

blocks.text: What forgetting Figma shortcuts costs you

The cost is small, and that is why it lasts. You stop to search a menu for a command you use every day. You drag a tool from the toolbar when one key would do. You open the wrong panel, then close it. Each detour takes a few seconds, and they repeat all day. I could not find a study that measures this for designers, so read this as a pattern to check on your own screen, not a fact about the whole field.

The bigger cost is attention. Figma work already asks you to make many small decisions about layers, frames and variants. Every menu hunt pulls you away from those decisions. Figma's design statistics page, citing a Monotype study from 2025, reports that 57% of creative teams spend more than a quarter of their time on non-creative tasks like file management and compliance. Shortcuts are a small slice of that. They are also a slice you can fix this week.
Figma keyboard shortcuts Mac: the keys to know first

Start with the keys Figma documents for itself. Its help article lists Mac and Windows pairs, and most pairs swap Ctrl on Windows for Command on Mac. Canvas zoom is one of them. The table below covers the keys you are most likely to need. Open the panel to check each one, because your version may differ from this list.

rows: Listed in Figma's help article. Check it in your copy of Figma.
Command on Mac, Ctrl on Windows, per Figma's help.
Option Space on Mac, per Figma's help.
Ctrl F6 on Windows, per Figma's help.
Search menu commands in most Mac apps
Apple's shortcut list. Opens Help menu search.
blocks.caption: Keys from Figma's help article and Apple's Mac shortcut list. Confirm each on your version.

blocks.text: Single-key tools are the next layer. Many Figma tools have one-letter shortcuts, and they are faster than the toolbar once they are automatic. Learn the ones you use most, such as the move tool and the frame tool. Confirm each letter in the panel before you lean on it, since a wrong letter can change your selection.
A worked example: relearning five keys in one week

Say you use Figma all day, but only a handful of commands do most of the work. Write those commands down first. Put the list on a sticky note on your second screen. On the first day, use the list for everything it covers, and use the mouse for the rest. Expect the first day to feel slow. That is normal. By the end of the week, your hand should reach for a key before your eyes find the menu.

Habit research gives a rough timeline, not a promise. A 2010 study by Lally and colleagues modeled how habits form in everyday life, mostly health behaviors. Its median was 66 days to reach a modeled plateau, with estimates from 18 to 254 days. Those are model estimates for health habits, not software. They still explain why a week can feel shaky. Plan for weeks, and keep the list short while you practice.
Set up App Shortcuts for Mac menu items

This is the one fix that lives on your Mac, not inside Figma. Apple says you can create your own shortcuts for any menu item. The setting sits in System Settings, under Keyboard. You bind a key combination to a menu label, and macOS uses that key when the app is active. The label must match exactly. Apple's page does not say which shortcuts cannot be changed, so test each one you add.

items: Open the menu in Figma and copy the exact label of the command.
Open System Settings, then go to Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts.
Select App Shortcuts, then click Add.
Choose Figma from the app list. If you run Figma in a browser, choose that browser instead.
Type the exact menu label, press the key combination, then click Add.
Open Figma, run the command with the new key, and check for a clash.

blocks.text: Two edge cases are worth knowing. First, when Figma runs in a browser tab, the menus you see belong to the browser, so the App Shortcut lives there. Second, not every Figma command sits in a menu. An App Shortcut needs a menu item to attach to. Test each shortcut before you trust it, and remove any that clash with a key you already use.
Figma shortcuts not working on Mac: clashes and layout

Sometimes the key never reaches Figma. Another app, a macOS shortcut or an input source may claim it first. Apple says every app can have its own shortcuts, and shortcuts that work in one app might not work in another. So test the key in a plain text box. If it fails there too, the clash sits outside Figma, and you need to change the shortcut that owns it.

Check the layout next. Figma has keyboard layout preferences in the Layout tab of the shortcuts panel. Figma's help says keyboard controls are on by default and cannot be turned off. If you type on a non-US layout, open that tab first. A layout mismatch can look exactly like a broken key, so rule it out before you change anything else.
Mistakes people make when they try to remember Figma shortcuts

items: Memorizing the whole panel on day one. Pick five keys, practice them, then add more.
Trusting an old cheat sheet. The Figma help article I opened shows no last-updated date, so check the panel after major updates.
Choosing a third-party sheet over Figma's help. One sheet lists the panel key as Shift Command question mark, while Figma's help says Control Shift question mark. Check the panel in your own copy.
Trying to remap Figma's own keys. Figma's help does not describe changing its shortcut keys. Use App Shortcuts for menu items instead.
Keeping the mouse route alive. If you always hunt the menu, the key never gets practice.

blocks.text: Why your Figma shortcuts slip on Mac

Shortcuts fade for a few reasons, and the fix depends on which one applies. Daily commands stick because you repeat them. Rare commands fade, so they need a written note more than repetition. Keys that live in a panel are easy to forget, because menus are always visible and the panel is not. Knowing which reason fits your case saves you from practicing the wrong thing.
What Lazur can and cannot do with your shortcuts

Lazur helps you find and learn the keys. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about anything on screen, such as where the shortcuts panel lives. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons or operate Figma for you. It is not a plugin for Figma, and it cannot set App Shortcuts on your behalf. Ask it to walk you through the System Settings steps, then do each click yourself. Check any key it names against the panel. A voice answer can miss how your version works.

Privacy works like this. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. If your Figma file is under an NDA, follow your studio's rules before you ask about it.
Where to go next with Figma on Mac

If the panel is the real problem, start with the desktop setup guide in [Figma for designers on Mac](/for/designers/figma). If shortcuts lag because the file is heavy, read [why a Figma file is so slow on Mac](/for/designers/problems/why-figma-file-so-slow-fixes). To practice one tool at a time, try [how to create a frame in Figma on Mac](/how-to/create-a-frame-in-figma).

If you also work in Photoshop, the Command key logic carries over, but the key sets differ. Keep a separate list for each app. The [Photoshop guide for designers](/for/designers/photoshop) covers that side of the workflow. Two short lists are easier to trust than one long one.

faq.question: Which figma keyboard shortcuts mac designers should learn first?
faq.answer: Start with the keys you use every hour, not a list from a blog. Figma's help article documents Command for canvas zoom, Option Space for box selection and F6 for the toolbar. Open the shortcuts panel with ⌃⇧? and pick five from your own work.

faq.question: Why does a shortcut work in one app but not in Figma?
faq.answer: Shortcuts belong to apps. Apple says shortcuts that work in one app might not work in another. Test the key in a plain text box. If it fails there too, another app or a macOS shortcut probably owns it.

faq.question: Can I change Figma's own keyboard shortcuts on Mac?
faq.answer: Figma's help article does not describe changing its shortcut keys. It says keyboard controls are on by default and cannot be disabled. For menu commands, you can add App Shortcuts in System Settings, which is the Mac-level route.

faq.question: Do App Shortcuts work when I use Figma in a browser?
faq.answer: Usually the browser owns the menus you see, so pick the browser in the App Shortcuts list. Apple's page does not describe this case, so test the key yourself before you rely on it.

faq.question: How long does it take to remember a shortcut?
faq.answer: It varies. A 2010 habit study estimated a median of 66 days, with a range from 18 to 254 days. That study covered everyday health habits, not software. Expect weeks of practice.

faq.question: Which cheat sheet should I trust for the panel key?
faq.answer: Trust the panel in your own copy of Figma. One third-party sheet lists Shift Command question mark, while Figma's help says Control Shift question mark. Your version is the final check.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or change Figma for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click, and it points at controls on screen.

faq.question: Is there a free trial before I pay for Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur has a Pro trial that needs no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Check [pricing](/pricing) for current plan details.

faq.question: What if my studio does not allow AI tools on client files?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut, and audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer. If your work is under an NDA, ask before you use it.

costs.title: Time lost to menu hunts
costs.text: Each menu hunt costs a few seconds. Repeated across a day, those seconds add up to real time. I found no study that measures this for Figma users. Track one day yourself by noting how often you open a menu for a command you should already know.

costs.title: Attention lost to switching
costs.text: Every menu trip pulls your eyes off the canvas. The switch is brief, but it breaks the thread of a layout decision. Figma's own statistics page reports that 57% of creative teams spend over a quarter of their time on non-creative tasks, which shows how much small friction builds up.

costs.title: Mistakes from the wrong key
costs.text: A wrong key can move an object, change a layer or open a panel you did not mean to open. Command Z undoes many of these, but some changes are easy to miss. Check the result of each key before you move on to the next step.

costs.title: Money, and what cannot be measured yet
costs.text: BLS reports a median annual wage of $62,960 for graphic designers in May 2025. Time lost to shortcuts is a small share of that, but it is real. The honest answer is that no source I found puts a dollar figure on it for Figma users.

causes.title: Habits from other apps
causes.text: Many designers learn shortcuts in one tool first, then carry those habits into Figma. Figma uses Command on Mac and Ctrl on Windows for many pairs, so a habit from one side can misfire on the other. Apple says every app can have its own shortcuts. Your hands follow the last app you used, not the one open in front of you.

causes.title: Rare commands fade fast
causes.text: A few commands run all day, and they stick. Rare ones fade, because you reach for them once a week or less. Habit research points to weeks of repetition, with a median of 66 days in a model of everyday habits. Rare commands need a written note more than repetition.

causes.title: The keys sit in a panel, not a menu
causes.text: Figma documents its keys in a shortcuts panel that you open with ⌃⇧?. If you look in menus first, you rarely see the key next to the command you use. The panel is the reference, but most people do not keep it open. App Shortcuts can add a second route for the commands you use most.

causes.title: Keyboard layout and macOS clashes
causes.text: A non-US keyboard layout can send different characters for the same key press. Another app or a macOS shortcut may claim the key first. Figma's help article says keyboard layout preferences live in the Layout tab of its shortcuts panel. The symptom looks the same in every case: the key does nothing, or it does something else.

causes.title: Cheat sheets that go stale or disagree
causes.text: Sources disagree on at least one Figma key. A third-party sheet lists the panel key as Shift Command question mark, while Figma's help article says Control Shift question mark. The Figma article I opened shows no last-updated date, so you cannot be sure it matches your version. Check the panel itself after updates.

causes.title: Reaching for the mouse out of habit
causes.text: A menu is always visible, so the mouse route feels safe. Each time you open a menu instead of pressing a key, the key loses a chance to stick. That gap grows over a week. The fix is not willpower. Pick a small set of keys, and treat the mouse route as the exception for those commands.

fixes.title: Open the shortcuts panel and read it once
fixes.text: Open the panel with ⌃⇧?, as Figma's help article describes. Read it once, top to bottom, without trying to memorize it. Note which keys you already know. The panel is the reference you can always check, so start there.

fixes.title: Practice five keys, not the whole list
fixes.text: Pick the five commands you run most often. Use only those keys for a full day. Keep the rest of the list for lookup. Small sets get practice, and practice is what moves a key into your hands.

fixes.title: Add App Shortcuts for daily menu commands
fixes.text: Go to System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. Match the menu label exactly. Test every new shortcut in Figma, and remove any that clash with another app. Apple's guide describes this path.

fixes.title: Check your keyboard layout first
fixes.text: Open the Layout tab in Figma's shortcuts panel. Confirm the keyboard layout preference matches the keyboard you type on. If a key behaves strangely, this is the cheapest check you can make, and it takes less than a minute.

fixes.title: Test a clash in a plain text box
fixes.text: Press the same key combination in Notes or another plain text field. If it fails there too, another app or macOS owns the key. Change or remove the shortcut that owns it in System Settings, then test again in Figma.

fixes.title: Use Help menu search for lost commands
fixes.text: In most Mac apps, ⇧⌘? opens Help search. Type a few words from the command name. Apple describes this as a way to search an app's menu commands. Use it when you forget a command, not as a daily habit.

fixes.title: Keep one list and check it after updates
fixes.text: Put your keys in one note. After a Figma update, open the panel and compare it with your list. The help article I checked had no visible update date, so do not rely on a date alone. Compare the keys themselves.

fixes.title: Ask Lazur, then confirm the answer
fixes.text: Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where a command lives. Lazur circles the control and answers out loud. Confirm the key against the panel before you add it to your list, since a voice answer can miss your version.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.title: Read the panel once
plan.text: Open the shortcuts panel with ⌃⇧? and read the list without trying to memorize it. Pick the five commands you use most. Write them on a sticky note or in Notes.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.title: Practice only those five
plan.text: Use the five keys for all your work today. Reach for the mouse on purpose only when no key works. Note any key that does nothing or does something else.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.title: Check layout and clashes
plan.text: Open the Layout tab in the panel and confirm your keyboard layout setting. If a key fails, test it in a plain text box to see whether another app or macOS owns it.

plan.label: Day 4
plan.title: Add App Shortcuts
plan.text: In System Settings, go to Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. Add one menu item you use daily, using its exact menu label. Test it right away in Figma.

plan.label: Day 5
plan.title: Ask Lazur one question
plan.text: Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where one command lives. Ask Lazur to guide you through it. Then check the key against the panel before you rely on it.

plan.label: Week 2
plan.title: Add five more keys
plan.text: Repeat the process with five more commands. Drop any key you never reach for. Keep the list short enough to fit on one note.

plan.label: After updates
plan.title: Re-check the list
plan.text: When Figma updates, open the panel and compare it with your note. Remove or change any key that moved. Cheat sheets go stale, so this step matters.
